newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL SUFFERS EARLY LOSSES ON HIGHER OFFER.
newsitem.headline: MOL SUFFERS EARLY LOSSES ON HIGHER OFFER.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian oil firm MOL lost some five percent in early trading on Monday as a result of a privatisation agency decision to raise the amount of shares to be offered to domestic investors, traders said.

MOL shares opened at 3,170 forints, well below the close of 3,335 forints on Wednesday, the last trading day in Hungary before a long weekend. At 0951 GMT it traded at 3,175 forints but traders expected it to recover after strong early sales.
"MOL's fall stems from the news of the one plus three percent share package on offer," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust. "But I think this panic will fade by the end of the day and it will recover."

Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt said last week it would raise the amount of MOL shares to be offered to domestic investors to one percent plus an additional three percent in case of strong demand.
Originally APV had planned to sell a one percent stake in MOL which could have been raised by another one percent.
In addition to the domestic offer, APV places 12.5 percent, with a 2.5 percent over-allotment option, with institutional investors privately.
